We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps correspond to forward reactions enumerated: 1) Carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). 2) Doebner modification (aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid). 3) Sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic steps reverse order: Starting from target, we break amide to give carboxylic acid and amine (step 1 reverse). Then break α,β-unsaturated acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). Then break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and amine.

Thus we need to find appropriate precursors: target has sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: a tolyl (para-methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonyl group attached to another phenyl bearing the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain.

So retrosynthesis:

Step 1 (reverse of amide formation): target -> precursor A (acid) + precursor B (aniline). The amide is C(=O)N attached to aniline (c3ccccc3N). So break amide: give carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline with NH2). The acid is the unsaturated acid: /C=C/COOH attached to phenyl sulfonyl group. So precursor A: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 (same but acid instead of amide). Precursor B: aniline (c3ccccc3N). Good.

Step 2 (reverse of Doebner modification): The unsaturated acid derived from aldehyde + malonic acid. The product is phenyl ring with /C=C/COOH attached (para to sulfonyl). The forward Doebner: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So reverse: break unsaturated acid into aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(C=O)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde is attached to phenyl ring that also has sulfonyl group. So precursor C: aromatic aldehyde with sulfonyl group: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(C=O)cc2)cc1 (i.e., same as target but aldehyde instead of unsaturated acid). Precursor D: malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Good.

Step 3 (reverse of sulfonamide formation): Break sulfonamide into sulfonyl chloride and amine. The sulfonamide is between tolyl amine (para-methyl phenyl with NH attached to sulfonyl) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl chloride (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl group attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc...). The sulfonyl chloride would be Cl-S(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(C=O)cc2 (or with aldehyde). So precursor E: sulfonyl chloride (Cl-SO2-aryl) where aryl is the phenyl bearing aldehyde. Precursor F: amine (p-toluidine) i.e., Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1.

Thus overall route: target -> (amide disconnection) -> unsaturated acid + aniline. Then unsaturated acid -> (Doebner) -> aldehyde-aryl sulfonyl + malonic acid. Then sulfonamide -> (sulfonyl chloride + amine) -> sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride) + p-toluidine.

We need to provide JSON with hierarchy: root molecule target, children reaction nodes etc. Each reaction node includes template_id. We need to find template IDs for each transformation. We have search results earlier: For sulfonamide formation, we saw template ID 1313644 (retro_smarts_template shows conversion of sulfonyl chloride + amine to sulfonamide). That seems appropriate. So reaction 3 (forward sulfonamide formation) corresponds to reverse step using same template. So we can use template_id 1313644.

For amide formation (carboxylic acid + amine -> amide), need a template. Search earlier didn't find. Let's search for amide formation template.
